key_insight: The more inferential steps a clinical question needs, the more likely large language models are to fail on EHR question answering.
clinical_relevance: Hop count may help flag which clinical AI queries are higher risk and need extra human review before deployment.
method: Annotated 313 clinician-generated MedAlign EHR questions with a pre-specified 4-level hop-count taxonomy.
Evaluated 301 questions across Claude Sonnet, GPT-4o, and GPT-5.4 under zero-shot and extended-thinking settings.
Compared accuracy trends by reasoning depth and checked whether EHR truncation explained the pattern.
evidence_signal: Across three models, accuracy fell steadily as hop count increased; for example, Claude Sonnet zero-shot dropped from 30.6% at hop 1 to 17.6% at hop 4, and similar monotone declines were seen in GPT-4o and GPT-5.4.
watch_item: This is a single-task, question-answering study, so hop count should be validated more broadly before using it as a deployment rule across clinical settings.
paper_title: Compositional Reasoning Depth Predicts Clinical AI Failure: Empirical Evidence Consistent with Transformer Compositionality Limits in Electronic Health Record Question Answering
